title: Board Policy 2023-01 terms for reusable dose planners and compliance packaging that the regulation does not state
subtopic: Compliance packaging and reusable dose planners: Board policy
rule_summary: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2023-01, Compliance Packaging and Reusable Dose Planners (adopted 4/6/23; revised 11/2/23 and 1/9/25; supersedes Policy 2022-08), restates the conditions of 247 CMR 9.07 and 9.08 and adds terms the regulation does not state. For a reusable daily dosage planner dispensed at the patient's or patient's agent's request, the policy lists as requirements that the pharmacy's policies and procedures include inspection of container integrity and drug accountability in addition to cleaning, labeling, dispensing and proper hand hygiene; that the medications are compatible with each other; and that the pharmacy does not dispense more than a 60-day supply of medication in a reusable daily dosage planner. For compliance packaging, the policy lists drug accountability among the subjects the policies and procedures for each type of compliance packaging include. The policy's multi-drug-single-dose packaging and return-and-repackaging passages each open with the words 'Unless otherwise prohibited', and the policy does not itself restate the prohibition in 247 CMR 9.08(3)(b) on dispensing Schedule II or III controlled substances in a multi-drug-single-dose package.
exam_relevance: Tests the difference between the regulation and dated Board policy: the 60-day planner supply, the compatibility condition for planners, and container-integrity inspection and drug accountability in the written procedures come from Policy 2023-01, not from 247 CMR 9.07.

authority.name: Policy 2023-01: Compliance Packaging and Reusable Dose Planners

numeric_facts.fact: Maximum supply in a reusable daily dosage planner under Board policy

common_confusions: Citing 247 CMR 9.07 for the 60-day planner limit, which appears in Policy 2023-01 rather than in the regulation.
Reading the policy's silence on Schedule II and III drugs in multi-drug-single-dose packages as permission.
verification_notes: Policy 2023-01 read in the mass.gov PDF linked from the current Pharmacy Practice Resources list (page header: Adopted 4/6/23; revised 11/2/23; 1/9/25) during the authoring session of 2026-09-16 to 2026-09-17, and compared with 247 CMR 9.07 and 9.08 in the 12/6/24 publication.
